summary:
Mission Sentinel is an interactive astronaut health-monitoring and research dashboard designed to support crew health and safety during long-duration space missions. It brings together astronaut physiological data, wearable-device telemetry, mission scenarios, and NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) research to help users explore health trends and identify potential risks.

The platform provides a unified view of vital signs, including heart rate, respiration, sleep, and other health indicators, alongside mission-related environmental information. It also includes scenario-based analysis, interactive visualizations, and a 3D anatomical reference to make complex health information easier to understand.

Mission Sentinel addresses the challenge of monitoring astronaut well-being in demanding space environments, where early awareness of physiological changes is essential. By connecting research data with an accessible monitoring interface, the project aims to support better-informed decisions and contribute to safer, healthier human space exploration.
details:
Project Details – Mission Sentinel

Mission Sentinel is an interactive astronaut health-monitoring and research platform developed to support astronaut safety during long-duration space missions.

How it works:
The platform brings together astronaut health indicators, wearable-device telemetry, mission scenarios, and NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) research. Users can explore physiological trends through an interactive dashboard, monitor indicators such as heart rate, respiration, sleep, and other health metrics, and examine different mission scenarios. It also includes interactive visualizations and a 3D anatomical reference to make complex health information easier to understand.

Benefits and Intended Impact:
The project aims to make astronaut health information more accessible and easier to interpret. By bringing different sources of information into one interface, it can help users recognize unusual health trends, explore potential risks, and understand the importance of continuous health monitoring in space. Its intended impact is to contribute to safer human space exploration and support research into astronaut well-being.

Tools and Technologies:
The project was developed using React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and JavaScript for the frontend with Python and FastAPI for backend services. We used NASA OSDR research resources, interactive data visualizations, and web-based development tools.

Creativity and Innovation:
The creative aspect of Mission Sentinel is its unified approach: instead of presenting health indicators, research information, mission scenarios, and anatomical references separately, it brings them together in one interactive environment. This makes the platform more engaging and helps users understand the relationship between astronaut health and mission conditions.

Factors Considered:
Our team considered astronaut safety, accessibility of scientific information, usability, clear data presentation, mission requirements, and the importance of identifying potential health concerns during extended spaceflight. We also considered how to make the interface informative, interactive, and useful for exploring space-health research.
